title: Tackling Federated Long-Tailed Learning via Synthetic Feature-Based Decoupled Training

problem.claim: Federated learning with non-IID, long-tailed data can produce biased models with degraded performance under privacy-preserving constraints.

gap.claim: Federated long-tailed learning requires methods that address local representation and decision-boundary learning while mitigating global model bias without sharing local training data.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Synthetic Feature-based Decoupled training (SFD) for federated long-tailed learning.
Adaptive Bi-Branch Learning jointly improves feature representation and decision-boundary learning during local training on non-IID long-tailed data.
Statistically Aligned Feature Synthesis generates privacy-preserving synthetic features approximating the global feature distribution for global classifier fine-tuning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show SFD effectively addresses federated long-tailed learning challenges.
The authors report superior performance on federated long-tailed learning datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning enables collaborative training on decentralized data without direct data sharing.
Long-tailed and non-IID data, combined with privacy constraints, can bias models and degrade performance.
SFD addresses the problem through ABBL for local training and SAFS for global classifier fine-tuning.
SAFS uses synthetic features approximating the global feature distribution, allowing classifier fine-tuning without sharing local training data.
The authors report extensive experiments and superior performance on federated long-tailed learning datasets.

source_observation.claim: Synthetic features approximating a global feature distribution are used to fine-tune a global classifier without sharing local training data.

interpretation.claim: Feature-level synthesis may provide a privacy-compatible way to reduce classifier bias when raw client data cannot be centralized.

application.claim: Consider privacy-preserving feature synthesis for distributed classification settings affected by client heterogeneity and class imbalance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how well the approach transfers to settings with different privacy constraints, feature distributions, or imbalance patterns.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not describe the privacy guarantees or threat model.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results for ABBL and SAFS.
